turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, come on through. Shame, you look done in. My sister was up half the night with her baby, so I'm a bit foggy myself, but we'll get you seen.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. Look, can we not drag this out. I hardly have the patience today.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Of course. Sit, please. I'm Doctor Naidoo. Tell me, what's brought you in?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I woke up and the left side of my face is just hanging. I can't whistle. It's, uh, ridiculous.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): That must have given you a proper fright. When did you first notice it?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): This morning, in the mirror. Maybe four hours ago. The alarm went and there it was.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the eye on that side, are you able to close it?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No. It won't shut. It keeps watering and it's irritating me no end.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. Any weakness in the arm or the leg?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Arms are fine. Legs too. I drove myself here.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. And your speech, any slurring, or words not coming?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I'm talking fine. I'm just tired and fed up, that's all.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any pain around the ear before the face went?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, yesterday. Behind the left ear, a dull ache. Still a bit tender if I press it.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): The parking outside is a nightmare, by the way. Took me ages.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ag, the lot is always full. With a droop that comes on this fast, my plan is to send you over for a brain scan this afternoon.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh for goodness sake. I cannot sit in casualty all day.
[SEG0018] person_1 (NURSE): Vitals are in, doctor, before you book anything. Blood pressure one thirty eight over eighty four, pulse seventy six, temperature thirty six point seven.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks. Let me examine you before I commit to that scan. Lift your eyebrows.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm trying. The left one just sits there.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): I see it. Forehead is flat on the left, the eye only closes about halfway, mouth pulls to the right, no arm drift, speech is clear.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): So it is a stroke then. My uncle had a stroke. Don't dance around it.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): I hear you. I'm actually changing that plan. The forehead is weak as well, which a stroke usually spares, and your arm and speech are fine. We are not doing the scan.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Then what on earth is it?

[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): This is a Bell's palsy. The nerve that moves the left side of the face has swollen inside a little bony tunnel by the ear. The swelling blocks the signals, so the muscles go slack. It is not a clot in the brain.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Swollen nerve. Wonderful. So I just walk around like this?
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): No. We'll start steroid tablets to bring that swelling down. Prednizone, sixty milligrams by mouth, once a day, for five days.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Sixty. I already take a blood pressure pill, amlodipine, five milligrams every morning. That won't clash?
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Amlodipine five milligrams is fine to carry on. Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing I know of.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good. Because the eye isn't closing, I'll give you carmalose drops, one drop in the left eye every two hours while you're awake.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Every two hours. Ugh. Fine.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): At night, tape the eye gently shut so it doesn't dry out. Don't drive if the drops make things blurry.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): How long is the face going to stay like this, honestly?
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): It often starts coming right over a few weeks. I want you back in one week to check the eye and the movement.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): And if it gets worse before that?

[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the arm goes weak, or the speech changes, or the eye gets very painful, go straight to casualty. Otherwise I'll see you in a week. Take the first sixty milligram dose today with food.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Are we finished?
[SEG0039] person_1 (NURSE): I'll print the script at the front desk. Go easy, hey.

clinical_assessment.assessment: Left Bell's palsy from swelling of the facial nerve in the bony canal, not a stroke
clinical_assessment.basis: Left forehead weakness, incomplete eye closure, mouth pull, no arm drift, clear speech, and ear pain since yesterday

clinical_actions.description: Start prednisone 60 mg by mouth once daily for 5 days
Start carmalose drops, 1 drop in the left eye every 2 hours while awake
Continue amlodipine 5 mg every morning
Tape the left eye gently shut at night and do not drive if the drops blur vision
Take the first prednisone dose today with food
Go to casualty if the arm goes weak, the speech changes, or the eye gets very painful
Explained that swelling of the left facial nerve in the bony canal is causing the droop and that this is not a stroke
Bell's palsy often starts coming right over a few weeks
Brain scan this afternoon was initially planned because the facial droop came on quickly, then the plan was changed after examination and the scan will not be done
Follow-up consultation

spec.situation: Person woke with one side of the face drooping, cannot close the eye, cannot whistle; no arm weakness, no speech problem, ear pain a day before; doctor examines and starts steroids, eye care explained.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
